stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Most vaccines teach the immune system to recognize a threat by exposing it to a weakened or inactivated version of the entire pathogen, so the body encounters dozens of the microbe's surface proteins at once. Subunit vaccines, ______ contain only a single purified protein from the pathogen, which is why they usually need an added ingredient called an adjuvant to provoke a strong enough response.
explanation: There are two subjects here: most vaccines, which present the whole pathogen and many proteins, and subunit vaccines, which present a single protein. The subjects differ and the attribute flips from many to one. That is a comparison-contrast relationship, so you need 'by contrast.'

A.why: You saw a specific kind of vaccine come after a general statement and took it as an illustration. Subunit vaccines go against the tendency described in the first sentence, because they do not use the whole pathogen. A case that breaks the general claim cannot be an example of it.

B.why: 'Similarly' needs the two subjects to share an attribute. A single purified protein is the opposite of 'dozens of surface proteins,' so the two sentences point in different directions.

D.why: You read a cause-and-effect link that the text does not contain. Whole-pathogen vaccines do not cause subunit vaccines to hold a single protein. The two are simply set side by side as different approaches.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Most planned towns built in the mid-twentieth century separated land uses, zoning homes far from shops and workplaces so that residents had to drive to run almost any errand. Veldmoor, a Dutch new town completed in 1974, ______ was laid out around a web of cycle paths that puts schools, stores, and the rail station within a short ride of nearly every house, while cars must loop out to a ring road to pass between neighborhoods.
explanation: The first sentence gives the usual pattern: planned towns built so that residents had to drive. Veldmoor is a planned town from the same era, but it was built so that residents could cycle to daily destinations. It reverses the usual pattern, so 'conversely' is the logical transition.

B.why: You chose an example word because one particular town follows a general claim about planned towns. Check whether the case agrees with the claim first. Veldmoor was designed around cycling rather than driving, so it goes against the tendency instead of illustrating it.

C.why: 'In other words' introduces a restatement of the same idea in different terms. The second sentence describes a different town with the opposite design, not a rewording of the first sentence.

D.why: Nothing in the passage says that other towns' car-centered zoning caused Veldmoor's cycle-path layout. You supplied a cause the text never states.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: P waves, the fastest seismic waves an earthquake produces, compress and stretch rock along their direction of travel and can pass through both the solid and the liquid layers of Earth's interior. S waves, ______ shake rock perpendicular to their direction of travel and cannot cross liquid at all. Their disappearance beyond a certain distance from an earthquake gave seismologists early evidence that Earth's outer core is molten.
explanation: The two sentences use the same frame for two kinds of wave. P waves move along the direction of travel and pass through liquid. S waves move perpendicular to it and cannot pass through liquid. The subjects differ and the key attribute flips, so 'in contrast' is correct.

A.why: 'Similarly' only works if S waves share the attribute given for P waves. P waves cross liquid and S waves cannot, so the two are opposites, not parallels.

B.why: S waves are not a sample of P waves or of anything the first sentence describes. They are a second, separate category with the opposite behavior. You treated a specific item as an illustration without checking whether it agrees with what came before.

C.why: P waves' ability to cross liquid does not make S waves move perpendicular or stop at liquid. The passage compares two wave types. It does not describe one causing the other.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Coaches in most endurance sports have their athletes taper, sharply cutting training volume in the final weeks before a race, because rested muscles typically produce faster times. Among the ultramarathon runners tracked by physiologist Lena Okafor, ______ those who tapered for more than ten days finished slower than those who kept training, apparently because very long races reward resistance to fatigue more than fresh legs.
explanation: The first sentence states a general rule: tapering usually produces faster times. Among Okafor's ultramarathoners, a long taper produced slower times. The specific case breaks the rule, so you need a contrast word, 'by contrast.'

A.why: This is the classic trap. A specific group of runners follows a general claim, so it looks like an example. But those runners got slower after tapering, which contradicts the claim that tapering produces faster times. An example has to agree with what it illustrates.

C.why: 'Thus' says the second sentence follows from the first. Slower times after tapering do not follow from a rule that tapering speeds athletes up. They cut against it.

D.why: 'Furthermore' adds a point in the same direction. Try the 'and also' test: 'Tapering produces faster times, and also tapering produced slower times' sounds wrong because the second idea contradicts the first.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Most dyers in medieval Europe guarded their recipes as trade secrets, passing formulas for fixing color to cloth only from master to apprentice and seldom committing them to paper. The dyers of the Flemish town of Oudenhove, ______ recorded their mordant formulas in a shared ledger that any guild member could consult, and several of its stained pages survive in the town archive today.
explanation: Most dyers kept their recipes secret and unwritten. The Oudenhove dyers wrote theirs down and shared them. These are two groups described with the same frame, and the attribute flips from secret to shared, so 'in contrast' is correct.

A.why: You reached for 'for example' because one particular town's dyers follow a claim about dyers in general. The Oudenhove dyers did the opposite of what most dyers did, so they are an exception, not an illustration.

C.why: 'In other words' introduces the same idea said more precisely. A shared written ledger is not a restatement of secret word-of-mouth instruction. It is its opposite.

D.why: 'Accordingly' marks a consequence. Other dyers' secrecy is not the reason the Oudenhove dyers kept an open ledger, so there is no cause-and-effect link here.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Baroque composers typically left ornamentation to the performer, writing only a bare melodic line and trusting skilled players to add trills and flourishes of their own. Johann Sebastian Bach, ______ wrote out many of his ornaments note by note, a habit that the critic Johann Adolph Scheibe attacked in 1737 for burying the natural beauty of a melody under too much detail.
explanation: The first sentence describes what Baroque composers usually did: leave ornaments to the performer. Bach did the reverse and wrote them out himself. Scheibe's criticism confirms that this was unusual. Because Bach's practice goes against the general tendency, 'by contrast' is correct.

A.why: Bach was a Baroque composer, so it is tempting to read him as an example of the group. But the passage presents him as doing the opposite of what the group typically did. Before you pick an example word, check that the case fits the general claim.

B.why: 'Similarly' would mean Bach also left ornaments to performers. Writing them out note by note is the opposite attribute, so an addition word misstates the relationship.

D.why: Other composers' habit of leaving ornaments to performers did not cause Bach to write his out. You read a consequence into two practices that are only being compared.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: The Mercator projection preserves the angles between lines on a map, which made it invaluable to navigators plotting a constant compass heading, but it enlarges landmasses more and more the farther they lie from the equator. Equal-area projections such as the Gall-Peters, ______ keep the relative sizes of landmasses accurate while distorting their shapes, stretching Africa and South America into noticeably elongated forms.
explanation: There are two subjects: the Mercator projection and equal-area projections. Mercator keeps shapes and angles but distorts size. Equal-area projections keep size but distort shape. The trade-off is reversed, so 'conversely' is the logical transition.

B.why: The phrase 'such as the Gall-Peters' already names an example within the second sentence, and that may have pulled you toward an example transition. But the transition has to link the two sentences, and equal-area projections are not an example of the Mercator projection. They make the opposite trade-off.

C.why: 'In addition' adds another point in the same direction. Here the second projection keeps exactly what the first one distorts and distorts what the first one keeps. That is an opposition, not an addition.

D.why: 'Hence' presents the second sentence as a result of the first. The Mercator projection's features do not produce the Gall-Peters projection's features. The passage sets two separate designs side by side.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Most field crops cannot reach high yields without large applications of nitrogen fertilizer, whether synthetic or from manure, because they draw nitrogen from the soil faster than natural processes replace it. Soybeans, ______ supply much of their own nitrogen: bacteria living in small nodules on their roots convert nitrogen from the air into a form the plant can absorb, so farmers often apply little or none.
explanation: The first sentence makes a general claim: most field crops need heavy nitrogen fertilizer. Soybeans are a field crop that largely does not, because root bacteria supply the nitrogen. The specific case breaks the general pattern, so 'by contrast' is correct.

A.why: Soybeans are a field crop, so they look like an example of the category in the first sentence. But the first sentence says field crops need heavy fertilizer, and soybeans need little. A crop that breaks the pattern cannot illustrate it.

B.why: Other crops' dependence on fertilizer does not cause soybeans to make their own nitrogen. The root bacteria cause that. 'As a result' invents a causal link the passage never draws.

C.why: 'Likewise' would mean soybeans also depend on added nitrogen. The passage says the opposite, so a same-direction word does not fit.
